failure_summary.description: The answer was a related setting, example, or candidate rather than the target specified by the clue or its full set of details.
The answer form was too short, included an unrequested role or rank, or used the wrong grammatical number.

patch.reasoning: The skill already covers target selection, full-clue evidence, and concise answer forms, so these edits sharpen those existing checks rather than adding new broad rules. They make demonstrative and category cues explicit, require candidate verification against all discriminating details, and clarify how to preserve canonical name and number while omitting unrequested qualifiers.

edits.target: Use distinctive details in the question—such as dates, roles, relationships, or defining descriptions—to find evidence that directly explains the full clue, rather than relying on a keyword-only match. If no single passage provides the answer, combine compatible details across relevant passages and corroborate the candidate when evidence is available. Ignore unrelated snippets.
edits.content: Use distinctive details in the question—such as dates, locations, actions, roles, and relationships—to find evidence that explains the full clue, not just a matching keyword. When multiple candidates or related entities appear, test each against all discriminating details and reject candidates that do not fit the complete description. If no single passage provides the answer, combine compatible details across relevant passages and corroborate the candidate when evidence is available. Ignore unrelated snippets.

edits.target: Before choosing a candidate, use the clue's head nouns and pronouns to identify the kind of answer requested: a manner, place, role, institution, species, person, or other category. Return that target, not a consequence, associated entity, or example used to identify it.
edits.content: Before choosing a candidate, use the clue's head nouns, pronouns, and demonstratives to identify the kind of answer requested: a manner, place, role, institution, species, person, or other category. In phrases such as “this play,” “this vitamin,” or “one of these [plural class],” return the work, substance, or class named by the phrase—not its setting, an example, or an individually numbered member—unless that detail is requested. Return the target, not a consequence or associated entity used to identify it.

edits.target: Use a name form that uniquely identifies the entity: give the complete identifying name when needed, but a surname or shorter form is appropriate when it is unambiguous.
edits.content: Use the context-supported conventional answer form: include the parts of a multiword identifying name when the shorter form is not canonical; shorten only when that form is conventionally used and unambiguous. Omit ranks or appositive role labels that merely qualify the answer, and preserve the source-supported conventional grammatical number rather than normalizing singular and plural.
